deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1967 notes for a lecture on crystalline cohomology. Here he summarises the Washnitzer–Monsky (W.M.) theory of 'formal' cohomology and states it in its sharpest form. Earlier pages set up the objects: W is a complete DVR with residue field k of characteristic p (e.g. Witt vectors), and K is its fraction field. W†{t_1..t_n} is the ring of overconvergent power series, i.e. series converging on some disc of radius ρ>1. W-M algebras (weakly complete finitely generated, or dagger algebras) are quotients of these rings by ideals, which are automatically closed.

The page states a conjectural theorem in three parts. W.M. prove a weakened variant of it.
(a) Existence of lifts: if A_0 is a finitely generated smooth k-algebra, there is a W-M algebra A over W, flat over W, with an isomorphism φ: A⊗_W k ≅ A_0.
(b) Uniqueness: such a pair (A,φ) is unique up to a (non-unique) W-isomorphism u: A→A' compatible with φ and φ'.
(c) Definitions: for a W-M algebra A, define Ω^1(A/W) by the universal property for derivations into finitely generated A-modules. Set Ω^•(A/W) = ∧^• Ω^1, a complex that is functorial in W-algebras. A homomorphism u: A→A' of smooth W-M algebras then induces u^*: H^i(Ω^•(A'/W)) → H^i(Ω^•(A/W)).

The next page completes the statement. It asserts that u^* depends only on the reduction u_0: A_0→A'_0, so H^•(Ω^•(A/W)) depends canonically only on A_0. It also notes that W.M. prove this only for 'special' A_0 and only modulo torsion (after ⊗K). Sheafifying over a smooth X_0 gives sheaves ℋ^*_{X_0}.

The purpose is to motivate p-adic cohomology for smooth affine varieties in characteristic p, as a precursor and comparison point for crystalline cohomology.
errors: Part (a) for arbitrary smooth A_0, rather than W.M.'s 'special' algebras, was not available in 1967. It was settled later via Elkik's algebraization and approximation results (1973) and subsequent work on dagger algebras.

The integral form of the claim (on the next page) is too optimistic as stated. W.M. established invariance only after ⊗K. The integral dagger de Rham cohomology has torsion pathologies, which is why later integral theories go through overconvergent de Rham–Witt complexes. Grothendieck himself flags that W.M. prove only the rational version, so this is a caution rather than a mistake on his part.

ideas.what: Existence of flat weakly complete (dagger) lifts of smooth affine k-algebras
ideas.where_published: Monsky–Washnitzer, Formal cohomology I (Ann. Math. 1968); Elkik, Ann. Sci. ENS 1973

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the lift up to non-unique isomorphism; lifting of morphisms
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of smooth dagger lifts (formal smoothness of weakly complete algebras)

ideas.what: Module of continuous differentials Ω^1(A/W) via a universal property for finitely generated modules; de Rham complex of the dagger lift; functoriality of its cohomology depending only on the reduction mod p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Monsky–Washnitzer; van der Put (1986) for a systematic treatment
ideas.where_published: Monsky, 'Formal cohomology II/III'; van der Put, Bull. SMF Mémoire 23 (1986)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an expository summary of Monsky–Washnitzer theory as it stood in 1967, with Grothendieck's sharper conjectural formulation. That formulation (general smooth A_0, integral invariance) was later partly proved by Elkik and van der Put, and is partly false integrally. Nothing here is new to specialists, though it documents Grothendieck's attention to MW cohomology in his crystal lectures.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'anto[?]contiguement[?] finis' should be 'automatiquement fermés)'. This completes the parenthetical '(les idéaux sont-ils automatiquement fermés)' from the previous page.
'Si A_0 est l.f. sur k et lisse sur k' should probably be 'Si A_0 est de t.f. [type fini] sur k et lisse sur k'.
'unique à isom (non unique pris)' should be read as 'unique à isom. (non unique près)'.
'∧^*(A/W)' should be read as the exterior algebra ∧^*Ω^1(A/W).
'un complexe fonct. en W-algèbres' should probably be read as 'un complexe d'algèbres, fonctoriel en les W-algèbres'.
The struck-out lines preceding the final statement concern 'u: A→A' commutant des...' and are deleted. The surviving text reads 'Soit u: A→A' un hom. de W.M.-algèbres lisses sur W, d'où u^*: ...'.
